{{Short description|Algebra term in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''double affine Hecke algebra''', or '''Cherednik algebra''',  is an [[associative algebra|algebra]] containing the [[affine Hecke algebra|Hecke algebra]] of an [[affine Weyl group]], given as the [[quotient ring|quotient]] of the [[group ring]] of a [[double affine braid group]]. They were introduced by [[Ivan Cherednik|Cherednik]], who used them to [[mathematical proof|prove]] [[Macdonald's constant term conjecture]] for [[Macdonald polynomial]]s. Infinitesimal Cherednik algebras have significant implications in [[representation theory]], and therefore have important applications in [[particle physics]] and [[chemistry]].
